hooks.text: On January 12, 1888, children walked to school without their coats.
Why did school children walk into an 1888 blizzard without coats?
A deceptively warm morning lured children into a deadly Arctic blizzard.

title: How Did the 1888 Schoolhouse Blizzard Trap Children? ⚠️
description: On January 12, 1888, a deceptively warm morning tempted Great Plains schoolchildren to leave their coats at home before a deadly Arctic blizzard struck.

beats.text: On January 12, 1888, children walked to school without their coats.
beats.visual: historical photograph of pioneer school children, 1888

beats.text: A deceptively mild morning had warmed the Great Plains.
beats.visual: photograph of a historical one-room schoolhouse on the Great Plains, 1880s

beats.text: Suddenly, an Arctic cold front plunged temperatures below zero.
beats.visual: historical map of Dakota Territory showing weather patterns, 1880s

beats.text: Blinding, powdery snow reduced outdoor visibility to zero.
beats.visual: archival photograph of massive snow drifts from the 1888 blizzard

beats.text: When schoolhouse fuel ran out, teacher Lois Royce led three pupils outside.
beats.visual: Venetian glass mural depicting the Schoolhouse Blizzard in the Nebraska State Capitol
queries: Schoolhouse Blizzard mural Nebraska State Capitol

beats.text: The children froze, and Royce lost her feet to frostbite.
beats.visual: archival photograph of a haystack on a snowy Great Plains prairie, 1880s

beats.text: At least 235 died in the Children's Blizzard.
beats.visual: historical photograph of winter storm damage, 1888

better_than_last: Designed a loop where the final beat's tragedy flows naturally back into the deceptive warm start of the first beat.
